title: Planet Zoo 2 is a beautiful sequel and a fine management sim, but it's the animals that steal the show
text:
If the Planet Zoo series has taught me anything it's that I'm rubbish at animals. Sure, I'm okay with the simple stuff - I do, you'll be relieved to hear, know the difference between an elephant and a flamingo - but the more exotic they get, the second we start dabbling in subspecies, the more clueless I am. That was one of the joys of the original Planet Zoo: a chance to discover a vibrant menagerie of unusual animals, all brought to wonderful life by developer Frontier's typically exquisite artistry. And after spending some early hours with Planet Zoo 2, it's this, as much as anything, that's kept me so completely enthralled.

Valor Mortis plays a bit of a sneaky trick. For a while it keeps it straight. 'Yes', it seems to say; 'I'm definitely a Soulslike. Look at my bonfire equivalents, my healing flasks, my corpse runs, even my early impossi-boss feints. Look at my cautious action, my fog gates, the oppressive air of melancholy that lingers over these fields of mud and blood'. But jumpcut to a few hours later, and there you are: first-person wall-running, grapple-swinging, one-two parry slashing, quick-step-fire-ball-dismembering, slow-mo bullettime high-jump shotgun-blast-to-the-face-ing. title: EA Sports FC 27 review
text:
The most touching of additions, in EA Sports FC 27, is a mode called The Grounds. This is an online social hub, where your custom avatar can roam and rise. It's touching not for its play – which lets you challenge people to rounds of Rush football, where the ghosts of Volta and Fifa Street happily haunt – but for its look. There are three open hub areas to explore, one styled on the UK, another on Paris, and a third on Argentina. The streets are clean, and cluttered by bustling NPCs. Here and there are luminous white-domed kiosks, with all the promise of an artist's impression of an upcoming Heathrow terminal. If I didn't know better, I'd say that the developers at EA Vancouver and EA Romania were paying homage to PlayStation Home. There, too, you could list through weird streets and glassy booths, clad in store-bought clothes, and beat other players in mini-games of all kinds. There, too, you felt the looming threat of a shutdown.

title: Epic Is Overhauling Its Anti-Cheat So That Fortnite Can Finally Come To A New Platform
text:
Thanks to devices such as the Steam Deck and Steam Machine, as well as the ongoing issues with Windows, gaming on Linux looks a lot more attractive over the last few years. Its biggest hurdle is still multiplayer games and their anti-cheat systems, but Epic Games is committed to bringing one of the biggest around to the operating system soon.

Epic Games has announced that it is working on a Linux version for Fortnite. It's going to act as a test for Epic's overhaul of EAC (Easy Anti-Cheat), its solution to those developing multiplayer games in Unreal Engine to prevent cheating (most recently used in Gears of War: E-Day). Epic says that it has offered Linux support for its current version of EAC, but that most developers (itself included) opted not to use it and instead omit Linux support entirely because of its inability to be as protective as its Windows version.

A native rebuild of EAC, that doesn't require translation layers such as Proton, would help Epic bring the software up to par with Windows, at which point it would be comfortable finally releasing a native Linux version of Fortnite. In a blog post, Epic says that once it has reached this stage, it will make this available to other developers, too.

"We are also planning to pilot EAC Linux v2 in Fortnite first, where we’ll test it in a live environment and refine it based on what we learn. Once we’ve validated EAC v2’s effectiveness, we’ll make it available to more game developers so they can bring their multiplayer games to Linux players too."

Epic hasn't shared a timeline for when it expects Fortnite on Linux, but does say that its pilot program will be available through its new Epic Game Store launcher. Announced at the same time, Epic has decided to follow through with its commitment to AI-developed software earlier this week, with the new launcher labelled as "vibe coded" because "programming is hard". This version is still in preview and lacks all of the features currently on the main version of the store launcher, but Epic says that it is already seeing some speed improvements (even if they're just a few seconds here or there).

That might be too steep a price to pay depending on your appetite for linking your credit card details to an app that is being iterated on without much (or any) human intervention. And it's already led to some strange bugs that certainly would've been caught without being rushed into the hands of users.

Earlier this week Epic Games reportedly delayed a Star Wars/ Marvel crossover title as the company pivots towards an "AI-first" production model that does away with "hand-written code."

title: Xbox Survey About Exclusives Includes A Nuclear Strategy, But Wait Just A Minute
text:
Microsoft is reportedly surveying a subset of Xbox users about changing its plans for exclusive games going forward--possibly in a big way--and that's no surprise given Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has alluded to changes to the exclusivity strategy in the future.

At the same time, a survey like this is not necessarily indicative of anything beyond Microsoft conducting research. After all, there is an entire team at Xbox called Xbox Research that ... researches all manner of things, and the results of that research doesn't always lead to changes in the marketplace.

Windows Central reports that a new survey was issued to some Xbox Insiders this week, and the site confirmed the survey to be real.

The survey asks how members might feel about the totally nuclear option of making all Xbox-developed games except Call of Duty exclusive to Xbox on console.

"Imagine it was announced that all future title releases from every Xbox-developed gaming franchise except Call of Duty will be console-exclusive to Xbox," the survey asks.

It goes on: "For Minecraft only, existing titles would no longer be available for purchase on PlayStation or Nintendo consoles and would not receive any new content updates. However, there is no impact to any of the existing titles or content you already own. Nothing changes on PC with this announcement."

The survey asks respondents to say in this scenario, where they would be most likely to play any of the exclusive content. The choices are:

  • On an existing Xbox I own
  • On a new Xbox Series X|S I would decide to purchase
  • On a PC
  • I would skip playing because it would now be unavailable on my preferred console
  • Something else
  • Not interested in playing the exclusive content

Another page of the survey specifically asks about Fallout, polling users about how they would feel if future Fallout games would be console-exclusive to Xbox, and with nothing changing at all on PC.

Windows Central reported that the survey also asked these same questions about The Elder Scrolls, Doom, Physint, Diablo, and Minecraft.

In a memo to staff, Sharma and Xbox boss Matt Booty said they will “re-evaluate” the approach to exclusivity, which could mean a lot of things. Surveying fans is likely connected to this endeavor.

Fans have called on Microsoft to return to exclusive games, but it remains to be seen if that will happen. Sharma and Booty also said they will consider changing things up in regards to “windowing,” which followed on from a report that said some other games beyond Call of Duty titles could be kept out of Game Pass at launch and for a period of time, similar to how movies are only available in theaters at first before coming to digital and streaming.

The so-called nuclear option of making all non-Call of Duty first-party games exclusive to Xbox on console would indeed be a bonafide return to exclusivity, but it also seems quite unlikely given how much money Microsoft could miss out on. At the same time, Sharma has pledged to fans that that Xbox needs exclusives to return to growth as part of the big Xbox "reset."

A survey like this offers an inherently hypothetical scenario, and it could simply be part of Microsoft's fact-finding mission to get a pulse of the fanbase. It would be an entirely different thing for Microsoft to commit to exclusives in this way and invest meaningfully to do so.

Sharma's other efforts so far as the new Xbox CEO have included mass layoffs, studio closures, and game cancellations. She has also said Microsoft's big bet on Game Pass did not work.

title: GTA 6 Reviews: When They Could Be Released
text:

Insider Gaming reported that reviews for GTA 6 will be posted at some point before November 19, but the exact timing is unknown for now. According to insider NateTheHate, Rockstar will send copies of GTA 6 to reviewers before the end of October, so any time now, seemingly.

This doesn't necessarily mean Rockstar will follow the same playbook for GTA 6, however. Nothing is confirmed at this stage.

GTA 6 launches on November 19--unless it's delayed again--for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. It's expected to be the biggest game of 2026 and maybe all time, and it's reportedly on pace to earn $2 billion in revenue before launch.

We also learned that GTA 6 did not in fact cost $1.5 billion to make and that an entire studio was spun up to create NPCs. title: Retro Handhelds Loaded With Unlicensed Games Could Face Government Crackdown
text:
The Electronic Software Association (ESA) has a serious bone to pick with retro handhelds that are packaged with tons of unlicensed pre-installed, calling these devices "superfakes" that should face some sort of suppression by the US government.

According to an October 6 filing with the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR)--which monitors marketplaces that are accused of engaging in or enabling piracy and counterfeiting--the ESA is urging the government to clamp down on what it calls "illicit plug-and-play consoles and handheld devices." The ESA wants the USTR to add these emulation devices to the Notorious Markets List, the agency's annual report identifying which markets are participating in such behavior, thereby barring or slowing their profits.

"In the video game sector, illicit plug-and-play consoles and handheld devices are the functional equivalent
of superfakes," the ESA told the USTR. "They can look and feel like legitimate, mass-market consumer electronics: molded housings, color displays, polished user interfaces, retail packaging, product reviews, warranty-like representations,
and listings on familiar e-commerce platforms. Yet their commercial appeal rests solely on a concealed
memory card or internal drive loaded with hundreds, thousands, or even tens of thousands of unauthorized
copies of copyright-protected games."

The ESA puts a specific spotlight on Anbernic, a console manufacturer that sells 3DS- and Game Boy-looking devices packed with thousands of games from systems like the NES and SNES to the PlayStation 1 and Sega Genesis. Though maybe the most prominent example, another one that comes to mind is rapper Soulja Boy's various console attempts.

The filing also targets digital marketplaces that it says distribute or sell modded accounts and pirated games such as Eldorado, FunPay, G2A, and Voices38. In short, the ESA is seeking some kind of restitution for the harm that "superfake" retro consoles pose to the gaming industry writ large.

"A single device can substitute for lawful purchases across multiple video game publishers and console generations, divert sales from authorized games, compilations, subscriptions, remasters, and licensed retro hardware," the ESA wrote. "Because the product is often delivered with an immediately usable catalogue of pirated games, it removes the technical friction that once separated mainstream consumers from video game piracy. Sellers commonly use the illicit library as a key selling point, and the commercial price often reflects this."

To achieve that restitution (or regulation), the ESA is "respectfully requesting" that the USTR implement the following seven steps so that the governments where these "superfakes" operate can hold their businesses accountable:

  • Treat preloaded unauthorised game libraries as core evidence of commercial-scale piracy
  • Inspect bundled and separately shipped storage media
  • Require sellers to substantiate authorisation for included games and protected branding
  • Suspend repeat sellers and linked storefronts, not merely individual listings
  • Preserve seller, payment, shipment, and advertising records for enforcement
  • Improve customs targeting for devices and components associated with preloading operations
  • Coordinate action against manufacturers, exporters, importers, fulfilment providers, and online marketplaces that knowingly facilitate these products

title: Ex-Overwatch Director Jeff Kaplan Says He Never Wanted The Spotlight, But The Game Needed A Face
text:
Being the face of a video game is a demanding role, as the people who step into these positions involved in these roles often find themselves on the receiving end of a lot of toxicity. Former Overwatch game director Jeff Kaplan knows this all too well, as he promoted the hero shooter for several years and regularly interacted with its fans--albeit at a "personal cost." 

After leaving Blizzard Entertainment in 2021, Kaplan has been quietly working on The Legend of California, the in-development game at his new studio, Kintsugiyama. Reflecting on his time as the face of Overwatch, Kaplan spoke to GameSpot about how Overwatch needed someone to fill that role. For Kaplan, this was part of Overwatch's growth and continued existence, and he felt it was needed at the time.

"This is going to sound ridiculous, but I'm not someone who likes attention," Kaplan said of his time in the public-facing position. "I'm not much of an extrovert. I don't have a heavy social media presence. And so, a lot of me putting myself out there when I was at Blizzard was sort of to serve my game and my team--doing a job and a role."

Overwatch--and Blizzard as a whole--has had tremendous highs and lows over the years. During periods of content droughts or Hero changes, players would often target Kaplan and other developers on the game with verbal abuse and threats. There has never been a silver bullet to eliminate player toxicity, but Blizzard discovered that dropping a ton of content into Overwatch helped change player sentiment.

While his departure from Blizzard back in 2021 wasn't easy, Kaplan said that being freed of the responsibility of being associated with Overwatch and fading into the background turned out to be "pretty great" in the end.

"There were a lot of emotions mixed up in leaving Blizzard, but one of the things that was sort of much needed for me, on a personal level, was that withdrawal," Kaplan said. "To stop reading the subreddits, to not talk to anybody. It's not like I had a game that I needed to talk to anybody about, and I don't have the need to see my name in headlines or, you know, like, 'Let's Google and see where I'm being mentioned today.' That's just not me as a person. So, it was very soothing to my soul to sort of fade into the background and just put all of that aside for some time. It was pretty great, actually. It was very needed for me."

Kaplan went on to explain his thoughts on if studios even need a  public face for their games, citing both Valve and Rockstar as companies that "do a great job of promoting their games" despite not having a designated speaker. 

"There doesn't need to be [one]," Kaplan said. "But I think it was good for Overwatch to sort of let the players know, 'We're one of you, we're listening.' It showed a level of transparency and engagement, like, 'Hey, this thing is being made by real people.' Blizzard always runs the risk of kind of, 'Oh, it's just a nameless, faceless corporation' if we don't put ourselves out there. 

"I think people like [current Overwatch director] Aaron [Keller] or myself, kind of [thought], 'Hey, we should really let these people know: We play the game too. We have opinions too.' That was sort of the strategy, but it comes at a cost to you personally. I know a lot of extroverts who love it and are like, 'I just did press for eight hours, and I feel energized!' And I'm like, 'Oh my god, I need to hide under a rock for seven days because I did one interview.'"

Currently, Kaplan and the rest of the team at Kintsugiyama are working on The Legend of California, a multiplayer survival-action game set in the wild west. The title doesn't have a release date yet, but if you're interested in taking part in an upcoming playtest for the open-world shooter, you can check out its Steam page and request access.

title: Jeff Kaplan Says Separation From Overwatch Was “Clinical”: ” I Never Go Back”
text:
Jeff Kaplan, Overwatch's former director, said he's not played the game he was the public face of since April 2021, when he left developer Blizzard after nearly 20 years to go indie. He called his relationship with Blizzard's shooter one of "clinical separation."

Kaplan revealed this to GameSpot in an interview that dove into his history with Blizzard and the creation of his new game, The Legend of California. 

When asked if he had continued to play Overwatch or kept tabs on it in the wake of it dropping the "2" from its name and its addition of 10 new heroes over the course of the year, Kaplan said he hadn't. He said he's essentially cut all ties with the game he used to direct.

"With Overwatch, I had a very almost clinical separation, knowing how the WoW thing had gone," Kaplan said. "I've literally not played the game since April 2021."

He continued: "I don't, for my own psyche, I don't read the subreddits. After I said my goodbye to competitive Overwatch and the Overwatch subreddit, I never go back and read. I don't watch YouTube [videos]. I don't search for my name in Overwatch. I don't search for Overwatch. I sort of just disconnect. I actually tell all the algorithms like, 'Yeah, I'm not really interested in Overwatch anymore. I know you think I'm the Overwatch guy, but like, that's just not for me anymore.'"

It was a lesson Kaplan learned when he left the World of Warcraft team in 2008 after working on Blizzard's MMORPG for six years. He said it was more painful to step away from WoW than it was for Overwatch.

"Oddly, leaving WoW was a training moment for me," he said. "When I left WoW to work on Titan [the game that would eventually become Overwatch], it was, I think, November or December of 2008. And WoW was who I was at that point. I worked every minute--every waking minute--on WoW. If I wasn't working on WoW, I was playing WoW. And every time I played WoW, I had this notepad next to the desk that I'd be filling out to walk in the next morning and go, 'These are all the things we need to change.'

"It was kind of shocking in a very negative emotional way to step away from WoW, because it was such a part of who I was and how I identified. It was who I was as a game developer."

As a result, when it came time to leave Overwatch and Blizzard behind, Kaplan said he was "used to that moment" of having given everything to a game, and the need to establish a "healthy separation" between him and his former work.

"I was kind of used to that moment of what it meant to give all of yourself, your heart, your soul--because it's not just a job, there's no one who can do this and have it just be a job--and then have this shocking moment where you realize it doesn't belong to you. It belongs to the team, belongs to the players, it belongs to Blizzard, but it doesn't belong to you," Kaplan said.

Kaplan said he was trying to avoid becoming Uncle Rico from the film Napoleon Dynamite, an old man reliving his glory days of playing football by watching tapes of his games.

"I don't want to be Uncle Rico," Kaplan said. "Overwatch happened. I was a part of it. There's a group there now and Overwatch is now about them. Both the players and the developers, that's their Overwatch now. They're making it, they own it, they play it. I'm onto this new thing, and that's where I'm at in my life."

title: Xbox Nano Controller Announced, And It’s So Small
text:
Microsoft has announced a new controlled called the Xbox Nano Controller, and it's smaller than the existing Xbox controller, and it costs less.

Microsoft says the controller is designed to fit nearly every pocket and budget. "Its compact design offers a great option for younger players, smaller hands, or anyone seeking something portable for play on the go," the company said.

The Xbox Nano controller is a bit over five inches in length and weighs 3.5 ounces--it's the smallest controller Microsoft has ever made. It features all 18 gameplay buttons you'd expect, so Microsoft says it should feel familiar.

The smaller controller comes with a smaller price, too: $50 USD. Microsoft partnered with Samsung on a bundle that comes with a controller and two months of Game Pass Ultimate (for new subscribers) when they buy a new Samsung TV this holiday. For anyone planning to use this new controller for cloud streaming, Microsoft will soon put caps on how much you can play before you must pay more to keep going.

Additionally, Microsoft and Facebook company Meta are working on a new bundle featuring the Nano controller, two months of Game Pass, and a Meta Quest headset.

The Xbox Nano controller uses rechargeable batteries and a programmable action button for quick access to things players want, like taking a screenshot or capturing gameplay.

You can preorder the Xbox Nano controller now. The Nano was the second new gaming controller revealed today, following Sony's announcement of a limited-edition DualSense controller for Gran Turismo.

title: Ubisoft’s Latest Restructuring Plan Puts Trials Developer RedLynx On The Chopping Block
text:
Ubisoft has announced that it plans to shut down Trials developer RedLynx as part of its ongoing restructuring efforts, as well as reduce the workforce of its Skull and Bones studio, Ubisoft Singapore, by laying off 72 people. The closure of the Finland-based RedLynx is in a proposal stage, and Ubisoft says that because the studio isn't currently working on a new project, it makes more economic sense to close it down and retrench its 52 employees instead.

Under Finnish law (via Kotaku), Ubisoft is legally required to consult and negotiate with employees before it makes major changes to the studio, which is why Ubisoft hasn't officially announced yet that it will shut down RedLynx--although it's likely only a matter of time. The studio was first formed in 2000, and it's best known for its series of challenging--but highly enjoyable--Trials games, 2.5D motorcycle platforming games that require players to master their vehicle, gravity, and overcome a series of increasingly dangerous obstacle courses. Ubisoft acquired the studio in 2011, and RedLynx's Trials HD quickly became a breakout hit on the Xbox Arcade marketplace.

Several games in the Trails franchise have been released over the years, with the last one being Trials Rising in 2019. Since then, RedLynx assisted Massive Entertainment with the Google Stadia port of The Division 2 and the Switch 2 port of Star Wars Outlaws, and it also produced the 2023 mobile game Gwen's Getaway. Last year, RedLynx lost 60 staff members during a restructuring wave at Ubisoft and it was announced that it would pivot to making mobile games.

Meanwhile, Ubisoft Singapore is projected to be losing as much as 20% of its workforce. Established in 2008, it assisted on development of several Assassin's Creed games and it was the lead developer on Skull and Bones, Ubisoft's naval warfare game set in the golden age of piracy. "At Ubisoft Singapore, 70 positions have been impacted to align the studio with upcoming production needs," Ubisoft said in a statement to GamesIndustry.Biz. "The studio remains an important part of Ubisoft’s global production organization. We deeply value the contributions of both teams and recognize the impact this may have on our colleagues. We are committed to supporting our teams throughout this process and conducting it with care and respect."

There have been several more big changes at Ubisoft recently, including the announcement that Rainbow Six Mobile will shut down in January 2027. As part of its Creative Houses restructuring, Creative House 2 has been confusingly rebranded to Massive Entertainment, while Massive Entertainment, the studio, will continue to exist within it. Ubisoft studios across Montréal, Paris, Sweden, and Toronto fall under this Creative House, which is focused on almost all of Ubisoft’s Tom Clancy-branded games.

title: GTA 6 Leaks Are Still Coming, Rockstar Labels The 2022 Hack “Weirdly Invasive”
text:
Rockstar Games has reacted to the mass GTA 6 leaks, which began in 2022, with a top developer at the studio saying it "feels like somebody's wading through your dirty washing." Bloomberg published these comments from Rockstar developers on the same day that GTA 6 leaker CyberLeek posted yet another gameplay leak, saying it could be the last.

"It feels like somebody’s wading through your dirty washing,” Rockstar North's Aaron Garbut said. “It’s like they’re inside your head. You see your early work out there. Nobody’s ever supposed to see that. It’s really weirdly invasive. And so it’s quite hard to deal with on an emotional level.”

Rockstar and Take-Two eventually tracked down the hacker who was allegedly responsible for the leaks in 2022. This person will reportedly face court on November 9, just days before GTA 6 releases.

The hack pushed Rockstar to implement a controversial new policy requiring developers to work from the office, as opposed to remotely. Rockstar publishing boss Jennifer Kolbe said Rockstar will take another look at this policy after GTA 6 is released, but she doesn't envision major changes.

"The idea that we would have the game in that many environments is something that I think the security team would not love,” she said. “I think if we did not have a game that people wanted to steal as much, maybe it would be an easier conversation.”

The major 2022 hack that led to a series of GTA 6 leaks was followed up by a new round of leaks this year from someone going by CyberLeek. The person, or group, was pushing a memecoin, but is apparently now shutting down. One final gameplay leak was published today, October 14, and it's a big one, so be aware of that when you're scrolling through your feed.

The Bloomberg story on GTA 6 included numerous other details, including how the game originally had a bigger scope and could have launched sooner, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick's response to a big delay, and the absurd amount of detail in the game.

The story also confirmed that GTA 6 did not in fact cost $1.5 billion to make and that an entire studio was spun up to create NPCs. We also learned from the story that Rockstar's GTA 6 realism experiment began with beer and sandwiches and that Rockstar won't need another eight years to release its next game.

GTA 6 releases on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, though it could be delayed again.

title: GTA 6 Could Have Been Even Bigger And Released Years Sooner, But Then These Things Happened
text:
A big new report revealed more details about Rockstar's long-awaited GTA 6, including how the game's scope was originally much bigger and that the game could have released years sooner.

Bloomberg reported that when a small team from Rockstar traveled to Miami in 2015 to begin planning GTA 6, they envisioned the game spanning "big swaths of land across both North and South America." It was in development under the codename Project Americas at this time.

The report went on to say that Rockstar would pare down GTA 6's scope to include Miami and its surrounding areas instead of the original ambition. It's not a small world, though, as GTA 6's map is 3X bigger than the map in Rockstar's last game, 2018's Red Dead Redemption II. In addition to GTA 6's version of Miami with Vice City, the game takes players to a range of other locations in greater Leonida, which is a stand-in for Florida.

The confirmed major locations in GTA 6 so far include:

  • Vice City
  • Leonida Keys
  • Grassrivers
  • Port Gellhorn
  • Ambrosia
  • Mount Kalaga

The report also digs into how Rockstar originally planned to develop GTA 6 concurrently with Red Dead Redemption II, which would have helped GTA 6 come to market sooner. However, as the scope for Red Dead Redemption II grew, Rockstar's Rob Nelson came to realize he needed to assign more staff at Rockstar's network of studios to help get the Western out the door in 2018.

According to Bloomberg, this meant GTA 6 would be delayed "several years," but one silver lining was how the work that went into Red Dead Redemption II would "pay off when we get to the game [GTA 6]."

Nelson pointed out that Rockstar, at one point in time, developed multiple games concurrently across offices, but now, Rockstar's network of teams work on one project together before moving on to the next.

Also in the report, Rockstar denied the rumor that GTA 6 cost $1.5 billion to develop, but did not provide any specifics on the actual cost. The game has reportedly generated $600 million in revenue through pre-sales and that number could rise to $2 billion before the game even releases.

GTA 6 was originally set to launch in 2025 before getting delayed to May 2026 and then again to November 2026. When Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick heard about the second delay, he said to Rockstar, "Please tell me you're kidding."

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, unless it is delayed again, which Rockstar has not ruled out.

title: Hideo Kojima Reviews 2026’s Most Divisive Movie, Digger
text:
After publishing his review of Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie, Hideo Kojima-who says his body is 70% made of movies--has posted his review of one of the most divisive mainstream films of the year. Yes, we're talking about Alejandro Iñárritu's satirical black comedy Digger, which stars Tom Cruise.

Kojima said Digger is a "film that all of us living in today's world should see."

He added: "It is a work that remains with the audience, provoking reflection and sounding alarms."

Kojima doesn't get into detailed specifics in his Digger review, and that's likely because, if you've seen the movie or know the plot, you wouldn't want to spoil the film for other people, either.

In any event, Kojima said Digger and its message will stay with you for years to come. "As you absorb this film and carry it with you, a 'tool (a digger)' for delving deeper into the future will surely begin to take shape within you," he said.

Kojima and Iñárritu' sat down with Gizmodo to discuss Digger and more--you can read the conversation here, but note that it's in Japanese.

Digger reviews are all over the place, and the film bombed at the box office, bringing in just $37 million globally thus far. The studio behind it, Warner Bros., leaned into the divisiveness, altering the movie's marketing campaign after reviews came out to encourage people to see it and decide for themselves.

As for Kojima, he’s keeping very busy with the upcoming games OD and Phsyint, both of which are in the works for Xbox. Physint will also be adapted for film and TV, while Kojima’s Death Stranding is coming to the big screen as well.

title: Take-Two CEO’s Response To Second GTA 6 Delay: “Please Tell Me You’re Kidding”
text:
Rockstar's GTA 6 is finally coming out on November 19, but the game was originally set to release in 2025. When the development team informed head of publishing, Jennifer Kolbe, that a delay to May 2026 was necessary, she made a call to Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick to let him know. Months later, she had to make that call again, informing Zelnick that a second delay to November 2026 was required to deliver Rockstar's full ambition for GTA 6.

His response? “I think he said, ‘You’re kidding. Please tell me you’re kidding,’” Kolbe told Bloomberg. “But once we talked through why, he got it."

Kolbe said she felt fortunate that Zelnick is "as reasonable as he is," because other executives might not budge and inform the team they need to find a way.

"We have been really, really lucky that we have not found ourselves in that place, because that happens to a lot of teams, and we’ve all played those games. It’s not great," she said.

For his part, Zelnick said said that for the most part, delaying a game is actually a "wise investment in time and financial resources" if the delay results in "the level of perfection it has the ability to reach."

GTA 6 is releasing on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, but another delay is not out of the question. Development head Phil Hooker said GTA 6 is "never completely settled," nor does Rockstar have an "exact blueprint."

"Even within the last few months, we’ve changed things," he said.

That being said, no one is expecting GTA 6 to be delayed any further. Take-Two will release its next earnings report on November 10, and the company is expected to reiterate the November 19 release date during that event.

GTA 6's physical copies, which include a code in the box and not a disc, will be available to buy at retailers on November 12, though the game does not unlock until a week later.

title: GTA 6’s Nightclubs Have An Absurd Amount Of Detail, Right Down To The Lighting
text:
How much detail is too much detail? In the case of Grand Theft Auto 6, developer Rockstar Games put an obscene amount of work into making the fictional city of Leonida as realistic as possible, including the nightclubs that players can frequent in the game. Those locations couldn't be pulled from thin air, and Rockstar embarked on several research trips to Miami to help inform the design of their party hubs, right down to the smallest detail.

Speaking to Bloomberg, artist Aaron Garbut revealed that the developers embarked on ridealongs with police officers, visited trendy nightclubs, and mingled with dancers at these establishments. The result of these excursions was that the Rockstar team could draw on a wealth of knowledge to create authentic hangout spots, with these locations featuring distinct animations and scripts for each patron, a bar full of unique drinks, and the studio even crafted lighting systems that work in sync with the music being played. "Layers and layers and layers of detail," as Garbut put it.

GTA 6 is hardly the first game to feature a nightclub as a destination, but these locations typically follow a fixed formula, and they serve as set dressing that seldom stands out. Hitman developer IO Interactive did raise the bar for just how good a nightclub location can be when it's designed in service of a game and a level, as seen in 007 First Light earlier this year--and Hitman 3's Berlin rave warehouse is also a pretty great example of mixing crowds, DJs, and elaborate lighting setups together.

But could GTA 6 raise the bar for this extremely specific segment of game design? So far, it looks like Rockstar has gone all in to make the game feel and look more immersive than anything else it has done before, even going so far as to create a studio focused exclusively on building non-playable characters. The proof will be in the nightclub pudding, so if you're planning on grabbing the game, it might be worth spending a few minutes in a two-drink-minimum establishment to soak up the atmosphere.

In more GTA 6 news, Rockstar is confident that you won't have to wait eight years to play its next game, and rumors of the game's budget just took a $1.5 billion hit.

title: Rockstar Says GTA 6 Didn’t Cost $1.5 Billion To Make, But Won’t Reveal The Real Number
text:
It's no secret that video game development is more expensive than ever before, and in a hit-driven industry, Grand Theft Auto VI is rumored to be the most expensive game ever made. Various numbers have been thrown around, with one report even claiming that $1.5 billion was spent--around the budget of Dubai's iconic Burj Khalifa skyscraper.

Speaking to Bloomberg, Rockstar shot down that claim, but it hasn't confirmed just how much investment it has taken to get the game over the finish line for its November release. With years of development behind it, multiple studios--including one Los Angeles-based division focused exclusively on NPCs--and scores of employees working on it, that final price tag is likely to be quite high, but it is expected that GTA 6 will quickly recoup its expenses and start generating some serious profits for Rockstar Games and its parent company, Take-Two Interactive.

The game has reportedly already sold 5+ million copies through preorders, generating more than half a billion dollars, and that number is expected to climb to 25 million preorders by launch day, pushing the numbers up to $2 billion. It's worth noting that preorders aren't guaranteed sales--Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick has commented on this--so these figures could always change.

Rockstar is already making bank without even selling the game, as the $400 GTA 6 collector's edition has also proven popular since it went up for preorder a few weeks ago--and it's a merchandise-only box of GTA 6 swag.

While Rockstar Games hasn't spoken about an online multiplayer component for GTA 6, it's rumored to be launching in 2027. Given how GTA 5's GTA Online mode reportedly brings in hundreds of millions of dollars in revenue each year, GTA 6's version of this mode is also expected to be a license to print money for Rockstar and Take-Two. But can GTA 6 pull people away from GTA Online? Valve veteran Chet Faliszek recently commented that it might be a hard sell, as many GTA Online players are heavily invested in the game and might be reluctant to give up a third space they have built over years.

No matter what choice Rockstar makes, it won’t please everyone, and it'll have to find a middle ground to keep as many players happy as possible. In related GTA 6 news, you can read about how Rockstar debated how realistic it wanted the game to be, and why the studio doesn't think you'll need to wait almost a decade for its next game.

title: Rockstar Built An Entire Studio Just To Create GTA 6 NPCs
text:
Rockstar Games reportedly established an entire studio in Los Angeles dedicated to creating NPCs for Grand Theft Auto 6 after realizing the game's ambitious world would need far more production resources than initially expected.

Speaking to Bloomberg, Rockstar development lead Rob Nelson explained that the team had struggled to meet its targets for the number of NPCs that needed to be written and animated. That makes sense when you consider how much more interactive they're reported to be, even noticing and reacting when you're carrying a weapon. The numbers were so concerning that they were a large reason for the first GTA 6 delay.

"The projections they were giving us were horrifying," Nelson said. To combat the issue, Rockstar subsequently built out a Los Angeles studio staffed with writers, producers, and directors who would exclusively focus on creating NPCs for the game. The decision was part of a wider effort to ensure the game would meet the studio's ambitious goals without sacrificing anything from its vision.

The sheer scale of that reflects Rockstar's approach to making the world of GTA 6 feel more convincing than ever. Instead of treating NPCs like background characters, the studio has worked to give the residents of Leonida more detailed behaviors and interactions.

Those lofty ambitions have contributed to GTA 6's lengthy development. It's been in production for more than eight years, with Rockstar having to navigate pandemic-related disruptions, changes in leadership, and decisions about how much realism to include.

Rockstar ultimately delayed GTA 6 twice, moving its planned release from 2025 to May 2026 before pushing it back again to November 19, 2026. Development lead Phil Hooker said that the team could have met an earlier deadline, but it would have compromised on the game it wanted to make.

However, the legwork in building a solid foundation for GTA 6 means that Rockstar says you won't have to wait another eight years for its next title.

title: Rockstar’s GTA 6 Realism Experiment Started With Beer And Sandwiches
text:
Compared to previous games in the series, Grand Theft Auto 6 is aiming to add new layers of realism to the franchise. As the criminal couple Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, players will explore a city where actions have consequences, and it's not easy to shake the long arm of the law when you cause chaos. It continues ideas that developer Rockstar Games began experimenting with in Red Dead Redemption 2, but the studio says it initially struggled to figure out how realistic it wanted GTA 6 to be while still offering a fun gameplay experience.

As detailed by Bloomberg's Jason Schreier, Rockstar had a foundation to build on for GTA 6, as it would once again be a satirical open-world game in which you could commit all manner of crime. But the small details proved tricky, as Rockstar Games wanted players to feel immersed in the game's world. At one point, the developers debated whether players would need to fetch a case of beer from a liquor store fridge and take it to the counter before they could buy it, or visit a supermarket to buy ingredients to make a stat-boosting sandwich. "Making each of these decisions required a lot of guesswork because so much of the game wasn’t yet finished," Schreier wrote.

By 2022, GTA 6 began to come into focus, even though much work remained on the ambitious game. "You go through a period where things don't work, but you see snippets," GTA 6 head of development Phil Hooker said to Bloomberg. 

From what Rockstar has shown off so far, GTA 6 appears to both look and feel realistic thanks to various gameplay systems. Characters will react to Jason and Lucia's antics, and the two protagonists are at the center of a relationship gameplay system that can let their partnership blossom romantically, or you can ignore it entirely and keep them as platonic partners in crime. Players won't feel "all-powerful" in the game either, as Rockstar boss Rob Nelson said that the world can react in a hostile manner to your actions.

GTA 6 releases on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and while a PC port hasn't been announced yet, it's rumored that it might arrive in Q1 2027.

title: Xbox Is Getting Into AI Gaming, Even If It Won’t Say So
text:
Vibe-coded games playable in web browsers have exploded in popularity recently, and amid a deluge of ports and remasters created with generative AI, Xbox is responding by creating Xbox Labs. The new branch of Xbox is described as an initiative designed to get more people playing games--especially on web browsers--but curiously, there's no mention of AI at all in the announcement.

"In recent weeks, we've seen games rapidly decompiled and rebuilt to run on hardware they were never originally designed to support," Xbox CEO Asha Sharma wrote. "Windows PC builds have been translated to run on Apple Silicon or ported to run inside a browser through WebAssembly and WebGPU, the latter now approaching 90% global browser support. Perhaps more surprisingly, we’ve seen many of the biggest games in the world have been remixed into the source code of another. These experiments challenge long-held assumptions about our industry: the tether between software and hardware, the boundary between creation and play, and how people discover and experience games."

Sharma added that Xbox CTO Scott Van Vliet and a small team have been tasked with turning "turn emerging ideas" into experiences for consumers and developers. The idea of banking heavily on AI to create games is still a controversial topic in the west--whereas Asian markets have heavily pivoted toward it. Dragon Quest creator Yuji Horii is a big proponent of the technology, and other studios have begun incorporating it into their workflows to help combat the rising development times and costs of making a video game in the modern age.

Xbox Labs could be an effort to change public opinion on AI, given that many of the projects popping up online are vibe-coded remasters of older games like The Simpsons: Hit and Run, or mash-ups creating a chimera out of IP like Minecraft and Elden Ring. Xbox's parent company, Microsoft, also has a stake in the AI arms race, as its significant investments in the tech have seen a surge in profits. Alongside Xbox Labs, the company also announced the formation of XP, a new subdivision dedicated to expanding Xbox's presence through film, television, and live events.

Unreal Engine and Fortnite maker Epic Games is also making a huge pivot toward an AI-first game-development model, and the company has reportedly delayed an unannounced shooter featuring Marvel and Star Wars characters.

title: Rockstar Says You Won’t Have To Wait Another 8 Years After GTA 6 For Its Next Game
text:
Rockstar has spent more than eight years developing Grand Theft Auto 6, but the studio hopes its next project will arrive considerably faster. Speaking to Bloomberg, Rockstar's head of development Phil Hooker explained how the company expanded its team and developed its technology for the hotly anticipated upcoming game, and how that'll make it easier to build future releases.

Hooker said the studio expects to benefit from the foundations established during the lengthy production of GTA 6. "The engine, the tools, and the team we've built during this project will allow us to do things more quickly," he explained.

He added that Rockstar wants to focus on expanding what it has already created rather than continually rebuilding its technology. "I feel confident that we can build on top of this and go more sideways than upwards to build more compelling content," he explained.

The approach should help Rockstar avoid another extended wait between major releases. GTA 5 launched in 2013, followed by Red Dead Redemption 2 in 2018. GTA 6, meanwhile, is scheduled to arrive on November 19, 2026, following a series of delays. Its development has seen significant changes to Rockstar's structure, with the company growing from 2,441 employees around the release of RDR2, to 4,711 staff across 12 offices.

There is a precedent for Rockstar building a new game relatively quickly by reusing existing technology. Grand Theft Auto: Vice City followed GTA 3 in less than a year. Rockstar's leadership hopes the studio can take a similar approach to future projects now that so much of the GTA 6 groundwork is complete.

Of course, Rockstar hasn't announced its next major game yet. The comments also don't confirm that the next title in the Grand Theft Auto series will arrive quickly, especially considering the scale of the studio's ambitions. Still, the systems built for GTA 6 will help Rockstar spend less time solving technical problems.

For now, Rockstar's attention understandably remains on GTA 6. The game is expected to be one of the biggest entertainment launches in history, with analysts predicting tens of millions of sales during its first few months.

title: Hideo Kojima Reviews The Resident Evil Movie
text:
Writer-director Hideo Kojima has seen Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie, and he has now shared his review. Kojima, a true cinephile known for his public movie reviews, said he "wasn't particularly interested" in seeing the movie at first, but he did, and he sounded pretty impressed by what he saw.

"Right from the opening, it hits you with music reminiscent of The Thing. From there, it’s a relentless barrage of classic horror techniques, terrifying situations, and jump scares that never lets up until the very end," he said.

Kojima went on to observe what others did as well, which is how the Resident Evil movie is more of a film that provides the "experience of playing Resident Evil" as opposed to watching an adaptation of one of its stories.

"It reminded me of how I felt when I first played the original Resident Evil on PlayStation back in 1996," he said. "I was just like [main character] Bryan in this movie. I kept getting game over after game over, shouting “F***!” over and over again. lol."

This is the kind of response that Cregger said he wanted viewers to have. It's also what got Cregger in some hot water with hardcore fans who wanted to see a straight adaptation of one of the games instead of Cregger's own original story set inside the world of Resident Evil.

Another bright spot for Kojima? While he was at the theater, he picked up some physical reading materials for the divisive new Tom Cruise movie Digger. A lot of people have had a lot of things to say about that film, and we are all waiting to hear what Kojima thought of it, whenever he sees it.

The new Resident Evil has made more than $320 million worldwide, following its big debut in China where it's made $40.7 million so far. Cregger's Resident Evil movie is now the highest-grossing entry in the series to date, surpassing the previous record-holder, which was 2016's The Final Chapter ($312 million).

For more, check out GameSpot's rundown of the highest-grossing Resident Evil movies of all time.

While Cregger has said he has ideas for another Resident Evil movie, he’s done with franchise movies and is instead making an original movie, The Flood, next.

As for Kojima, he's keeping very busy with the upcoming games OD and Phsyint, both of which are in the works for Xbox. Physint will also be adapted for film and TV, while Kojima's Death Stranding is coming to the big screen as well.

title: Battlefield 6 Now Lets You Instantly Unlock All Guns At 100% Mastery For $30
text:
It's a big week for Battlefield 6, as the game just launched its big Season 5 update, arrived on Xbox Game Pass, and ushered in a new Game of the Year Edition. That's not all, however, as the military shooter added a big new microtransaction in the form of the Ultimate Shortcut Kit.

Similar to how these shortcut kits worked in past Battlefield games, Battlefield 6's $30 no-so-microtransaction instantly unlocks all of the game's guns for all four classes, and at 100% Mastery--this means they are fully leveled up and kitted out.

title: Despite Huge Changes For The Series, Halo Fest 2026 Is Going Forward, And News Is Coming Soon
text:
The big Halo Fest event planned for December is going ahead as planned, despite mass layoffs and other major changes at developer Halo Studios.

Halo Studios director of competitive engagement, Tashi, confirmed this and said there will be news about Halo Fest this week. Additionally, Halo Studios will release materials "celebrating the community and 25 years of Halo," while fans can also look forward to "relevant game info" about in-market Halo games.

"There's a huge amount of Halo fans who are looking forward to the event to attend or watch from home, and we're looking forward to providing a platform for the community to celebrate 25 years of Halo and each other," Tashi said of Halo Fest.

Halo Fest takes place December 11-13 in Seattle--the event is totally sold out. "No matter why you love Halo, whether it’s the story and characters, the music, the art and universe, or just playing with friends--Halo Fest will have something for you," Microsoft said of the event.

The voices of Master Chief and Cortana, Steve Downes and Jen Taylor, will appear at Halo Fest, while there will also be a range of community events celebrating the series. Some had expected Halo Studios to announce the next big Halo game at Halo Fest, but it's not unreasonable to think that plans may have changed.

Halo Fest is happening against a major shift for the Halo franchise following the gutting of Halo Studios and the transition of the series from Halo Studios to Activision. Halo Studios now employs a significantly smaller team that will support already-released Halo games like Halo: The Master Chief Collection and Halo Infinite, but future games in the series--including the rumored reboot--will be made at Activision.

Halo Studios was rumored to be working on Halo 2 and Halo 3 remakes, as well as a new live-service Halo game. That was before the big changes, however, and it's been reported that Activision is working on a Halo reboot.

title: Red Dead’s Shocking Twist Ending Angered A Lot Of People, But It Was The Right Call, Rockstar Co-Founder Says
text:
Rockstar co-founder Dan Houser has recalled the controversial ending to 2010's Red Dead Redemption in which the main character, John Marston, is killed.

He said in an interview that the game's lead designer, Christian Cantamessa was on board with the idea to kill off Marston, but Houser wondered about the production realities of, "How does an open-world game work if you've killed the protagonist?"

"So I said, ‘I think maybe we have to kill him.’ And he goes, ‘That's a great idea. Got to do it.’ I said, ‘I don't know if… let me just think about this,’ because we're just dealing with audio and dialogue," Houser told IGN "The nature of an open-world game is you finish a story, then you go back into the world and wrap up all the side content if you want to. We'd have to play as someone else for that. We could play as Jack, but what does that mean? So I had to think through for a while what it would mean production-wise.”

How Rockstar handled it was by setting RDR's epilogue years later, in the year 1914, with players taking control of Marston's son, Jack. He said this setup presented challenges, too, in terms of the technical realities of playing as Jack as opposed to John. There were story and mission concerns, too, including how multi-stage missions might play out if players, as John, completed one part and then came back to finish later as Jack.

"How would that work? We had to think through all of that stuff and concluded we could probably make it work, but we were still scared," he said.

The RDR epilogue has Jack hunting down and killing the men who killed his father, and Houser said players "really loved" that feeling of vengeance. Ultimately, Houser observed that there was "broad consensus" that it was the right call in the end to kill off John, even if it was an "unusual and out-there decision." Houser was, however, surprised by "how angry some people were about that decision."

"There were people who were livid with you. And part of you goes, ‘That's fantastic,’ because it means you've really engaged in the story and the characters," he said. "Now, I think it was the right decision because you want those big, strong reactions, but I think people were really confused by it. As a writer, it was like he had to die for the story to have any weight."

Also in the interview, Houser said he wanted to achieve something like this in the GTA franchise, but it never happened due to technical reasons.

He and the Rockstar team did, however, pull it off again with Red Dead Redemption II, which is a prequel to the earlier game. RDR2 famously killed off its own main playable character, Arthur Morgan, though he died from tuberculosis or at the hand of Micah. RDR 2 had an epilogue as well, featuring John and Jack Marston.

Houser left Rockstar in 2020 and now works at Absurd Ventures, which is crafting an open-world comedy game. His brother, Sam Houser, remains at Rockstar and helped lead the team bringing GTA 6 to market on November 19.

title: Battlefield 6 Comes To Game Pass, Game Of The Year Edition Announced
text:
It's a big day for Xbox Game Pass, as developer Battlefield Studios has launched Battlefield 6 into Game Pass, and it comes at a big moment for the game.

Battlefield 6 is now available for Xbox Game Pass Ultimate ($23/month) subscribers on PC and console. It can also be streamed.

The game's arrival in Game Pass is notable because Battlefield 6 was 2025's best-selling game overall in the US, and was released a year ago this month. The game had a very strong start, but player numbers have dropped. Battlefield Studios is attempting to reignite the fanbase in a number of ways, including bringing the game to Game Pass and continuing to support the FPS with big new updates. The latest of these, the Season 5 update, is out today, October 13.

Season 5 adds a new maps, including environments set in Las Vegas and Area 51, while it also brings something fans have been asking for since launch: a proper server browser. Check out the gameplay trailer above to see the Season 5 content in action.

Additionally, Battlefield Studios announced a Game of the Year Edition for Battlefield 6. The biggest selling point for the GOTY edition is the Ultimate Shortcut Kit, which instantly unlocks everything for all four classes, along with one season of Battlefield Pro, among other digital perks and extras.

The Ultimate Shortcut Kit, which was also available in other previous Battlefield games, is available to purchase by itself for $30.

title: God Of War’s Laufey Collector’s Edition Leaves One Important Thing Out: The Game
text:
The God of War Laufey Collector's Edition has been revealed, but unlike the standard and digital deluxe editions that went up for preorder last month, this is purely a box of merch. The main attraction of this collector's edition is an eight-inch statue of Faye, Phranque the Cube, and Rue fighting against Begtse’s soldiers. Phranque will light up when connected to a USB power source.

The set also includes a deck of 51 illustrated oracle cards and a mini art book depicting the characters, creatures, and environments of God of War Laufey, all housed in collector's edition-packaging. As noted in the image, God of War Laufey is sold separately, and this edition costs $150. You'll need to shell out another $70 for a physical edition of the game to complete it. Preorders are now live on the PlayStation Direct Store ahead of the game's February 2027 release.

Sony has released several collector's editions in the past that bundled a digital download key for a game. A merchandise-only box set isn't uncommon, as just a few weeks ago, Rockstar Games revealed the $400 GTA 6 collector's edition that comes with plenty of stuff.

So what's the thinking behind one of these boxes? These boxes typically target dedicated, high-spending superfans who can afford to shell out extra for bonus physical content like this, acting as high-margin merchandise. At the same time, publishers can save some cash by not including the game, streamlining their supply chains and lowering production overhead in the process. Essentially, a bigger slice of the pie for companies, while consumers with deep pockets get limited-edition swag to display.

In other God of War news, the next game in the series will see Kratos return to the spotlight, and it'll pick up directly after the end of God of War Laufey. A live-action God of War TV series is also in development for Prime Video, and its new leading man, Dave Bautista, is already working to get shredded for the role after the original Kratos actor, Ryan Hurst, departed due to injury.

title: Xbox Is Testing A New Streak Feature That Could Make Gaming Feel (More) Like A Chore
text:
It looks like another new Xbox feature is in development, and this time, it's designed to encourage users to go on a hot streak--of using their console, not disrupting a sports event with a quick birthday-suit-run.

Spotted by Game File's Stephen Totilo, a new number appears to be popping up on the dashboard of Xbox users who are signed up for the Xbox Insider program, suggesting that a streak counter is in development. Microsoft hasn't formally announced this feature yet, and it looks like it kicks in after using your Xbox for three days in a row per week. It's an idea that Microsoft has experimented with in the past through Game Pass and the Xbox mobile app, but never to this extent with a prominent display of how many days in a row you've dedicated to playing Xbox games.

Is there any benefit to Streaks for Xbox users? Totilo's research suggests that it could be tied to Xbox reward points, which can be redeemed for digital items and Xbox gift cards. On Microsoft's side, this could also be a subtle way to keep users engaged more consistently, since the lure of a score streak is powerful. Just look at Wordle, with its subtle emphasis on keeping your streak going, or mobile free-to-play games that offer daily login rewards to tempt you to sign in regularly.

That could be good, bad, or irritating depending on how it is implemented, as Xbox users could find themselves regularly pinged on their progress while they're in the middle of a game. Your tolerance mileage might vary when it comes to these notifications, so hopefully there's an opt-out option if Streaks roll out. But as Totilo noted, just because Xbox is testing this new streak function doesn't mean it'll be implemented across the Xbox ecosystem in the future. The fine print for Xbox Insiders mentions that these features may not become "permanent additions" to Xbox.

One new addition to Xbox that has been confirmed are Mythic Achievements, which are designed to be proof of your accomplishments in a given video game. Similar to PlayStation Platinum Trophies, a Mythic Achievement is earned whenever all of the original achievements for a game have been earned.

title: GTA 6 Will Reportedly Come To PC Much Earlier Than Expected
text:
The November launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 will leave PC gamers sitting out in the cold, but the wait for the yet-to-be-announced PC port might be surprisingly short this time. According to a new report, GTA 6 will launch on PC "within the first three months" of 2027.

Speaking to GamesBeat, industry sources claim that Rockstar Games plans to launch the game just a few months after its console release. If the reports are accurate, this would mark a major departure for Rockstar Games, as previous PC ports arrived long after their original console releases. GTA 5, for example, landed on PC 18 months after its PS3 and Xbox 360 release, while the PC version of Red Dead Redemption 2 appeared 11 months after its PS4 and Xbox One release.

Take-Two Interactive boss Strauss Zelnick previously commented that PC was becoming an important platform for the GTA 6 parent company to focus on, saying sales of the publisher's PC games had increased dramatically over the years. 

As for why GTA 6 won't be available on PC at launch, former Rockstar producer John Ricchio theorized that a console-first approach to development would give Rockstar more room to build a PC version later. Since consoles have limited hardware, it's easier for a studio to expand a game to run on more powerful hardware like a PC instead of scaling back to fit console constraints.

Rockstar hasn’t officially said anything about GTA 6 on PC yet, and the game officially lists only PS5 and Xbox Series X|S as its platforms. Xbox also recently clarified that GTA 6 will not be streamed to PC through Xbox Cloud Gaming, despite initial reports that Microsoft had secured exclusive streaming rights.

title: GTA 6 Fans Are Excited For Another Date In November, And It’s Not Release Day
text:
Take-Two has announced the details for its next earnings briefing, and as you might expect, GTA 6 fans are circling the date on their calendars.

The next Take-Two quarterly earnings report will be released on Monday, November 9, with management holding a call at 1:30 PM PT / 4:30 PM ET that day to discuss the results and answer questions. Anyone can listen to the call online.

The report is being released 10 days before GTA 6 launches on November 19, so it's expected that analysts and investors will ask questions about the upcoming launch. Management, including CEO Strauss Zelnick, will likely have some kind of update or commentary to share.

However, fans should not hold out hope for any big details about the game itself, as those kinds of details historically come by way of developer Rockstar Games.

The next Take-Two earnings report is expected in February 2027, but if GTA 6 is the enormous success that everyone expects it to be, the company will likely share details about the game's commercial impact before then.

For GTA 5, Take-Two announced sales right away, confirming $800 million in revenue after the first 24 hours and $1 billion in revenue after three days.

If Sensor Tower's data is accurate, GTA 6 has already sold more than 6 million copies via pre-purchases, bringing in close to $600 million in revenue. Sensor Tower said the game could reach 25 million preorders by release, meaning the game will have made more than $2 billion before launch.

Take-Two investors are understandably excited about GTA 6's release, but the game stands to make even more money once the next evolution of GTA Online launches. To be sure, Rockstar has not yet announced any details about GTA 6's online component, and GTA 6 has been described as a single-player experience.

That being said, given the gigantic success of GTA Online in terms of popularity among fans and its moneymaking ability, it's a safe bet that Rockstar will bring online functionality to GTA 6 at some point.

Beyond any possible updates about GTA 6, the Take-Two earnings report and following call is expected to include updates on the company's numerous other franchises and studios. After all, the GTA franchise represents a very small part of Take-Two's overall business, accounting for less than 15% of total revenue. That number is for a typical quarter–when GTA 6 launches, it will significantly increase.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.
